steps.title: 4 GiB of LPDDR4, drawn to scale, in two views
steps.body:
The board's RAM starts at `0x4000_0000` and ends at `0x1_3FFF_FFFF`. The top bar shows the whole RAM while Linux runs; the bottom bar zooms into the first 64 MiB to show what happens during `booti`, U-Boot's kernel-launch command.

Values come from this board's boot log and U-Boot environment.

steps.title: The kernel sits near the start of RAM
steps.body: The kernel's 35 MiB of code and data lives at `0x4060_0000`, 2 MiB aligned, just above the base of RAM.

steps.title: 256 MiB are reserved for the GPU
steps.body: A fixed block at `0x6000_0000` belongs to the graphics hardware. Linux cannot hand it to ordinary processes, which is one reason the memory Linux reports is less than the full 4 GiB.

steps.title: Another reservation holds the audio DSP firmware
steps.body: Near `0x9240_0000`, about 31 MiB are set aside for the HiFi4 audio DSP firmware and its heap. Without the reservation Linux could overwrite code the DSP is running.

steps.title: Bounce buffers serve 32-bit DMA devices
steps.body: Some devices can only do DMA (direct memory access, reading RAM without the CPU) below 4 GiB. When such a device needs memory that is higher, Linux copies data through this 64 MiB bounce buffer.

steps.title: A 704 MiB CMA pool serves big contiguous buffers
steps.body: The Contiguous Memory Allocator keeps one large block free for GPU, VPU (video) and camera buffers, which need physically contiguous memory. It runs up to the 4 GiB boundary and ordinary pages may use it until a device asks.

steps.title: The 4 GiB line splits DMA and Normal zones
steps.body: Below `0x1_0000_0000` is ZONE_DMA, above it ZONE_NORMAL, ordinary RAM. This line is why 32-bit devices need the bounce buffers.

steps.title: During booti, files land at fixed addresses
steps.body: SPL (1) and U-Boot at `0x4020_0000` come first, then U-Boot (2) reads `Image.gz` (14.9 MiB) to `img_addr = 0x4200_0000` and the device tree (78 KiB) to `fdt_addr = 0x4300_0000`. These addresses are U-Boot environment variables you can print.

steps.title: The kernel is unzipped, moved and run
steps.body:
The compressed image is unzipped to `loadaddr = 0x4048_0000` and moved to `0x4060_0000` (2 MiB aligned). The 34.2 MiB Image then runs there, spanning `0x4060_0000` to `0x4290_0000`.

Note the SPL and BL31 live in on-chip RAM (`0x0092_0000` and `0x0097_0000`), not in DDR; an OP-TEE build would also reserve `0x5600_0000` to `0x57FF_FFFF`.
